prompt: A scroll-driven explainer: as the reader scrolls a 4000px article, four illustrations appear and the heading changes. The entry file is `main.eligian` in the current directory, with one timeline named `story` that follows the scroll position of the element `#article` (the scrollable element, whose content is 4000px tall) and has a duration of 100s. Use these element ids: `#article`, `#heading` and `#illustration-1` to `#illustration-4`. The illustrations appear at 15s, 40s, 65s and 90s (`#illustration-1` at 15s, `#illustration-4` at 90s); each is hidden before it appears and stays visible from then on, up to and including the very end of the article (position 100s). The text of `#heading` is exactly `Where it begins` from 0s, `The turning point` from 40s, `What it changed` from 65s and `Where it goes next` from 90s up to and including position 100s. An element counts as hidden when it or an ancestor has the `hidden` attribute or computes `display: none`, `visibility: hidden` or `opacity: 0` from your CSS; otherwise it is visible.
